name: tikv-jemallocator (jemalloc global allocator)
baseline: System allocator: macOS libmalloc (rustc builds), glibc 2.43 malloc, musl malloc
verdict_reason: On macOS, rust-lang measured cargo and toml-rs builds 13-14% faster once rustc's jemalloc was actually wired in, and on musl it avoids the slow default allocator. On glibc the picture is mixed: jemalloc 5.3.0 was faster on lean and espresso but slower on redis and 3.5x slower on the cross-thread xmalloc test, and ripgrep's author found no meaningful difference for its workload.
tier_reason: The rust-lang project measuring rustc with hyperfine, plus an independent mimalloc-bench run; the rustc numbers come from two runs per configuration.
claimed_speedup: rustc with jemalloc on macOS: cargo build 66.658 s vs 75.251 s ('1.13 ± 0.01 times faster'), toml-rs build 5.968 s vs 6.777 s ('1.14 ± 0.01 times faster'). mimalloc-bench, jemalloc 5.3.0 vs glibc 2.43: leanN 0:07.78 vs 0:09.05 and espresso 0:02.97 vs 0:03.23 (faster); redis 0:2.619 vs 0:2.240 and xmalloc-testN 2.573 vs 0.739 (slower).
workload: Building cargo and toml-rs from scratch with a nightly rustc whose allocator was or was not jemalloc (hyperfine, 2 runs each); mimalloc-bench allt suite on glibc.
hardware: Intel Mac, model not stated (rustc); Intel Core i7-13800H (mimalloc-bench)
os: macOS on x86_64-apple-darwin (rustc); Ubuntu 26.04 with glibc 2.43 (mimalloc-bench)
toolchain: nightly-2021-03-08 vs the next nightly with PR #82642 (rustc); -march=native (mimalloc-bench)
platforms: Linux (x86_64, aarch64, powerpc64le tested), macOS (aarch64 tested), musl; not Windows MSVC
one_liner: Maintained jemalloc bindings that rustc itself uses; 13-14% faster rustc builds on macOS, mixed results against modern glibc.
how_it_is_fast: Per-thread caches serve small allocations without locks, and memory is spread over several arenas to cut contention. The Rust wrapper passes the allocation size to sdallocx on free, which skips a metadata lookup that plain free() needs.
use_it_when: Static musl builds (ripgrep switches to it on musl for this reason)
macOS programs whose allocation is heavy, as with rustc
Long-running services that need jemalloc's heap profiling and statistics
skip_it_when: glibc Linux programs that are not allocation-bound: ripgrep saw no meaningful difference
Producer-consumer patterns that free on another thread, where jemalloc 5.3.0 trailed glibc on xmalloc-test
caveats: The macOS numbers are two runs each on one unnamed Intel Mac, measuring rustc rather than a typical Rust program.
In 2021 rustc linked jemalloc through the jemalloc-sys crate; it switched to tikv-jemalloc-sys later.
mimalloc-bench runs C programs built with -march=native, not Rust.
tradeoffs: Longer build: jemalloc is compiled from C source; ripgrep's author notes it increases compile times.
Different memory profile: in mimalloc-bench redis peaked at 8156 KB vs glibc's 6324 KB.
